title: Former GM, Worldwide Business Development at Super Micro Computer Inc. Sees Asia Vital Components Maintaining Share Through Rubin Amid Growing Liquid-Cooling Demand
expert: Head of AI Infrastructure at Global AI (AI-server buyer, ~20,000 GPUs/yr); former GM, Worldwide BD at Super Micro
verdict: AVC parts sit in ~70% of the ~20,000 GPUs the expert deploys a year (his own BOM audits), often picked when default vendors would slip weeks to a quarter.

Rubin yield and ramp: 🟢 Rubin yield ~80% now vs 60–70% early 2026 (hearsay), up from ~60% in May (SB #64479). → Tenet 1 (Rubin content and share) ↑
🟢 Field cold-plate failure rate below 2% (first-hand), first read; quality is the share risk he names.
Nvidia content and share: 🟢 AVC in ~70% of ~20,000 GPUs a year (first-hand presence, not share), consistent with JPM's ~50% per AI project (SB #58861). → Tenet 1 (Rubin content and share) ↑
🟢 Liquid cooling 80% on GB300 to >90% on Rubin (estimate), first read.
Gross margin: ⚪ No cold-plate price declines seen; OEMs absorb any switch premium, consistent with JPM's ASP raises (SB #58857). → Tenet 3 (GM 34%+) →

changes: Rubin cold-plate yield ~80% (hearsay) vs ~60% in May (SB #64479) and 40-45% end-April (thesis page): improving.
AVC present in ~70% of the expert's GPUs vs ~30% Nvidia GB cold-plate share (SB #64467): different measures; consistent with JPM's ~50% per project (SB #58861).
No cold-plate price declines seen vs JPM: AVC raised ASPs on switch-tray cold plates (SB #58857): consistent.
thesis_impact: Tenet 1 (Rubin content and share): ↑ — AVC in ~70% of ~20,000 GPUs a year; Rubin liquid adoption >90% vs 80% on GB300.
Tenet 3 (GM 34%+): → — no price declines seen; standardization pressure flagged but unquantified.
Tenet 4 (capacity): → — only allocation mismatches could move volume; no numbers.
